title: Scalar-Tensor Hydrodynamics: Gravity as the Response of a Vacuum Medium. A Modified Gravity Framework for Vacuum Viscosity and Cyclic Vacuum Cosmology
description:
A theoretical proposal built on one premise: there is no empty space. The vacuum is treated as a single continuous medium, the Ocean, with its own stress-energy, pressure and internal flow, and with no edges and no outside. What are conventionally called particles are treated as localized excitations of the medium, and gravity is proposed to be the medium's response to concentrated energy. The medium has one speed, at which every disturbance travels. No speed is fixed: the measured speed of light is the local carrying speed read by rulers and clocks made of the same medium. Einstein's equation is retained as the effective description of that response.

Two principles of the framework, that the medium stays in step and that nothing is counted twice, give General Relativity's geometry outside a non-spinning mass, including its point of no return and the observed size of the shadow of Sagittarius A*. Around a spinning mass, a pattern's surroundings are re-made as it travels and tilted by its travel; summed over the Earth's spinning parts they give the frame dragging measured by Gravity Probe B, LAGEOS, LARES and LARES-2, carried continuously by the re-made state. Beyond first order the medium's rulers stretch by direction, so that a spinning hole's outside is General Relativity's.

Version 3.12 adds the rebuild and the law. The medium rebuilds every pattern continuously, and the rebuild has two sides: building, which makes matter and time, and reclaiming, which unmakes them and is antimatter. Time is made in the build, each place making its own, and gravity is the uneven making of time. Antimatter stays hidden because it runs into a past that was never a present; visible antimatter is a reclaiming with no build of its own. At the end of a beat the drive runs out and the reclaiming carries the medium, taking away time, structure and disorder and returning the energy. The law states what a build carries and the rule for each quantity, and sets the strength of gravity by a count of the kinds of wave the medium sustains: with fifteen built per family gravity attracts and the medium's smallest scale lies near the Planck length. It commits to one prediction, neutrinoless double-beta decay. The electron's 0.511 MeV is the lowest energy of its own kind of wave, set by a field the medium's flow sustains. The open items are gathered in one section. Version 3.12.1 adds Appendix A, the rebuild of a spinning black hole: Sagittarius A* taken through the same steps as the Earth's rebuild, with a table comparing the two regimes; it is also issued as a standalone PDF.

Version 3.13 decides how the medium's behaviors divide between its flow and the rebuild. The rebuild supplies the medium's current as it expands, so there is no separate rate of the phase to set, and nothing moving through the medium feels drag: gravity is the uneven making of time, not a current slowed by drag. The Ocean-wide waves that carry the rebuilt state are given a law built from twists alone, tested seven ways: its frame part is the teleparallel equivalent of General Relativity, and it carries light, the other carriers, the field that joins the two hands, and matter as half-angle waves, with exactly three families. A galaxy sits in an eddy of the medium far larger than itself, whose own energy adds to what the galaxy's stars read; its strength is set by the galaxy's mass and one limit held at every eddy's center, which gives the baryonic Tully-Fisher and radial acceleration relations and has not followed the slowing of the expansion over eleven billion years. Version 3.13.1 makes five wording corrections found in an independent reading, with no result changed. Appendix B follows the Milky Way's eddy, which carries the Earth and holds the black hole at its center.

Version 3.14 is a corrections release: each change removes something the framework had borrowed or misstated. The microwave background is read as the medium's heat, its normal component, left from the beat's beginning. The phase's law is written in the build's terms with no outside clock: the settled medium keeps its energy per volume exactly, has no wave of its own, and falls freely into every mass from rest far away, carrying nothing in; the horizon is where the rebuild uses the medium's full capacity. An eddy is held between each build's inward lean and the pushback of builds at work holding the medium's energy on loan, in place of a support borrowed from the standard account of a halo; its limit is the most one place can have on loan, set by the settled medium's own energy per volume, the fraction not derived. The eddy acts through the energy of the build in it, not an energy of its own; the loosening of the medium's grip at extreme density is the framework's own, and the form used to illustrate it is attributed to loop quantum cosmology; the searches for a sterile neutrino are named as a test, and the two-beam search finds none. The abstract is shortened and the revision account cut to its highlights. Every part of the paper carries a checksum token.

Version 3.15 gives the medium's grip its own form: at each place it is the part of the medium's capacity not already drawn, read at the width of its smallest scale, so collapse stops and turns before any singularity; the same expansion equation arises in loop quantum cosmology for its own reasons, and is cited as such. It follows a beat's turn and the beginning of the next in a new Appendix C: reclaiming alone, everywhere at once, with the energy kept as heat; the settled medium forming again out of the heat; and the build building with nothing to trigger it, its first builds making pairs. Hawking radiation is given in the rebuild's terms: each place's build keeps that place's own clock, and a clock far away reads the mismatch as a thermal glow; a traveler falling in meets a faint glow, about four times the far temperature at the crossing. The one constant in the phase's law is read as the energy of the medium's flow, which comes from the builds and powers only the plexus. 3.14's reading of an eddy's limit as the most one place can have on loan is withdrawn, since the Earth's builds hold far more on loan at the Earth's own place; every build in an eddy holds its own loan, and the flow's energy, acting through the plexus, remains the candidate for the common amount at every eddy's center. An eddy is given a beginning: one of the medium's rivers, its builds bent round bound matter and held; bound matter that no river has reached shows no extra turning, as the galaxies NGC 1052-DF2 and DF4 do. The paper was read independently before release. Every part of the paper carries a checksum token, and a reading manifest with a document digest (a3b9-ab23-4d9c) lets any reader confirm a complete reading.

This is a proposal, not an established theory. The document states its own falsification conditions explicitly and carries an itemized research program, several items of which could terminate the framework.
